name: WORD MELT
title: WORD MELT
challenge: Observer loss & cognitive fusion
moment: Observer loss & cognitive fusion
mechanism: Choose Charged → Listen Moment → Return Seen
goal: Hear one charged word as sound instead of carrying its whole story — loosen old pattern.
steps:
1. Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop there and look around the room.
5. Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

name: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
challenge: Communication & conflict
moment: Communication & conflict
mechanism: Read Bandwidth → Send Signal → Set Reopen
goal: Fit the conversation to the amount you can safely handle right now — loosen old cycle.
steps:
1. Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

name: THEN AND NOW, NO STORY DETAILS
title: THEN AND NOW, NO STORY DETAILS
challenge: Trauma & memory-as-present
moment: Trauma & memory-as-present
mechanism: Memory-as-present confusion family: say then was past opens a route toward end comparison.
goal: Shorten current loop: separate what happened then from the options available to you now.
steps:
1. Say, “That happened then,” without describing what happened.
2. State your exact present location and today's date.
3. Name one freedom or option available now.
4. Identify who can help in the current day.
5. End after one comparison and return to the room.

name: ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT
title: ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT
challenge: Achievement keeps moving the finish line
moment: Achievement keeps moving the finish line
mechanism: Body-state misreading family: identify part opens a route toward choose non.
goal: Find what is already adequate, then choose one improvement without desperation; interrupt tight orbit.

2. Receive that adequacy without claiming everything is fine.
3. From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.

name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
challenge: Catastrophic prediction
moment: Catastrophic prediction
mechanism: Pin Forecast → Score Odds → Update Odds
goal: Unhook mental loop: make fear state exactly what should happen, by when, and how confident it is.
steps:
1. Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Use the prediction a real time window.
3. Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Use the result to update confidence in either direction.

name: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
challenge: Panic & body alarm
moment: Panic & body alarm
mechanism: Read Channels → Move Dial → Check Panel
goal: Interrupt stuck pattern; change only the quietest safe channel of body alarm and leave the louder ones alone.
steps:
1. Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

45–60 seconds

GOAL
Leave familiar spiral: park a problem until the missing information needed to think usefully actually exists.

STEPS
1. Name what is missing: another person’s decision, a test result, a future opening, or a resource.
2. Name what change would make thinking useful again.
3. Until that happens, store the problem with that trigger and stop working it.

WIN
The missing information got a clear reopening trigger, so the problem no longer needed constant mental work.

RETURN KEY
Loop hooks · PARKWHAT
PARKWHAT · State Change
PARKWHAT · Store Away

MIND BEND
Thinking cannot solve information that does not exist yet. Repeating the calculation only creates more versions of the same gap.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Variable → State Change → Store Away

SAFETY
PAUSE
Continue any preparation that remains possible while the variable is unavailable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
title: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
challenge: Attention & cognitive overload
moment: Attention & cognitive overload
mechanism: Cognitive overload family: assign concern opens a route toward mark undeliverable.
goal: Unhook old orbit; route a returning concern to one real destination or mark it undeliverable.
steps:
1. Assign the concern to one place: a named person, calendar slot, document, task name, or deliberate release.

3. If no useful address exists, mark the thought UNDELIVERABLE and let it pass without rerouting.

name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
challenge: Action avoidance & procrastination
moment: Action avoidance & procrastination
mechanism: Run Pulse → Read Strain → Set Gear
goal: Exit old orbit: find a work-rest gear that matches actual strain instead of your prediction about strain.
steps:
1. Pick one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Unhook mental spiral; use real evidence of past progress to choose the next realistic step.

STEPS
1. Find three real changes from earlier effort: speed, quality, recovery time, knowledge, frequency, or distance.
2. Add a date or example to each.
3. Pick one next step that is now realistic because one of those changes exists.

WIN
Three real signs of progress made one next action feel supported by evidence rather than hope.

RETURN KEY
HARVEST / Orbit tightens
HARVEST / Date Examples
HARVEST / Choose Action

MIND BEND
Progress disappears when you compare only with the final goal. Looking backward can reveal abilities that have already changed.

FORMULA FLOW
Create Prior → Date Examples → Choose Action

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not cherry-pick progress to ignore deteriorating health or strategy.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE

name: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
challenge: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
moment: Evidence distortion & selective thinking
mechanism: State Rule → Compare Effects → Keep Core
goal: Disrupt mental orbit; move one inherited rule across different settings and keep only what remains ethical and workable.
steps:
1. Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Retain just the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Disrupt mental orbit; move one inherited rule across different settings and keep only what remains ethical and workable.

STEPS
1. Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Retain just the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

WIN
The rule changed meaning across family, work, and friendship, revealing which parts were universal and which depended on context.

challenge: Ignoring hunger, messages, or time while absorbed in the moment
moment: Ignoring hunger, messages, or time while absorbed in the moment
mechanism: Verbal naming + micro-action interrupts context loss by moving the move toward a clean stopping point.
goal: Carry the unfinished context through a one-minute move instead of losing it during the transition — shorten current cycle.
steps:
1. Name one drifting moment.
2. Label the unfinished context.
3. Give the coming sixty seconds your awareness.
4. Take one tiny response on the work already underway.
5. Label what changed after that minute.

name: A WIDER HORIZON
title: A WIDER HORIZON
challenge: A role has started defining your whole identity in the moment
moment: A role has started defining your whole identity in the moment
mechanism: Micro-action + attention shift interrupts role fusion by moving the horizon toward a wider sense of self.
goal: Interrupt familiar cycle; widen identity beyond the role that is currently taking over.
steps:
1. Name the role that is taking over your sense of self.
2. Name two parts of you that exist outside that role.
3. Pick one priority that is yours, rather than the role’s.
4. Take a tiny action that expresses that wider identity.
5. Keep one piece of evidence that you are more than the role.

name: SET ONE ROOM
title: SET ONE ROOM
challenge: You are close to drinking, using, gambling, bingeing, or another impulsive action in the moment
moment: You are close to drinking, using, gambling, bingeing, or another impulsive action in the moment
mechanism: Attention shift + micro-action interrupts high-intensity urge by moving the room toward distance from the urge.
goal: Disrupt automatic pattern: treat the strong urge as non-commanding and make access safer before deciding anything.
steps:
1. Say, “Strong urge, no command.”
2. Use a 10-minute delay before the usual action.
3. Silence one avoidable input or trigger.
4. Move to a safer place or surface away from easy access.
5. Contact live support if the urge still feels hard to manage safely.

PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Keep only the boundary or request that remains true after the angry rush is separated from it; interrupt mental loop.

STEPS
1. Pause before you send anything.
2. Describe the physical rush with a compact label.
3. Compare the angry prediction with one current fact.
4. Hold only the factual boundary or request you still stand by.
5. Send nothing until you can say it in the shortest real sentence without a threat or insult.

WIN
The message stayed unsent until the factual part could be expressed briefly without threat or insult.

RETURN KEY
Cycle grabs → COOLFIRST
Slow Hands → COOLFIRST
Say Simply → COOLFIRST

MIND BEND
The shortest defensible sentence often reveals the actual issue. Extra heat can feel like emphasis while secretly changing the purpose of the message.

FORMULA FLOW
Postpone Move → Slow Hands → Split Facts → Keep Edge → Say Simply

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not send, drive, confront, threaten, or act while control feels reduced. Move away from weapons and hazards; use human or emergency support if anyone may be unsafe.
This is brief self-help, not treatment or emergency care.

challenge: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify

goal: End self-investigation and move toward a familiar person or staffed safe place.
